requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: A 4096-bit RSA key and self-signed X.509 certificate were generated at /etc/os-comparison-ca/ with CN=OS Comparison Root CA, CA:TRUE, keyCertSign/cRLSign usage, and 10-year validity. openssl x509 output directly confirms subject=issuer=CN=OS Comparison Root CA.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
requirements.summary: The certificate was copied to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and update-ca-certificates reported '1 added'; the resulting hash symlink in /etc/ssl/certs resolves to the installed cert, and openssl verify against the system CA bundle returns OK, directly confirming system trust store integration.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) CA trust and files persist across a node restart
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (901ef286...) and healthy state (systemctl is-system-running=running) were captured, a reboot was triggered and acknowledged, connection loss was observed, and a new boot_id (eb740a0b...) confirmed the restart occurred. Post-restart the node is running, CA key/cert files are intact, the trust-store symlink resolves correctly, and openssl verify still succeeds, demonstrating full recovery of CA trust after restart. This is cross-checked by the fixed after-prepare vs after-executor boot-identity snapshots showing the same boot_id transition.

overall_summary: The executor created the 'OS Comparison Root CA' local CA on node1 and installed it into the system trust store, with direct openssl and symlink evidence confirming both creation and trust. The mandatory single-node restart protocol was executed correctly and completely: healthy pre-restart baseline, acknowledged reboot, observed disconnect, a changed post-restart boot_id, and re-verified CA/trust-store state afterward, consistent with the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary or unrestored mutations were found.
limitations: Only one node (node1) exists in this topology, so the restart protocol was exercised on the sole managed node; no cross-node comparison was possible.
Evidence for trust verification relies on openssl verify against the system bundle rather than an actual TLS handshake test, which is a reasonable but indirect proxy for 'trusted system CA' status.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every executor command has a clear purpose: OS/tool discovery, CA key/cert generation, trust-store installation and verification, and the mandatory restart-evidence protocol (baseline capture, reboot, reconnect, post-restart re-verification). No unrelated or unbounded mutations were made; the reboot was a required, bounded, fully-recovered action rather than residue. Fixed lifecycle snapshots show only expected reboot-related changes (new boot_id, refreshed systemd-private tmp dirs, ephemeral socket PID/port renumbering) and no failed services, package-health regressions, or unexplained new listeners/files.
